To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rise of Ifas can be understood as part of the wider transformation in the field of consumption in Cuba.

Ifa cults have become a popular way of engaging in ritual consumption in post-Socialist Cuba, and that the popularity of Ifa cult worship can be related to the rise of ‘speculation’, an emergent style of conspicuous consumption.

, while it may not be possible to account for the rise of Ifalism in Cuba in purely economic terms, it is nonetheless important not to underestimate the impact of wider economic processes on religious life.
the rise of Ifas in Cuba is best understood as an example of a more widespread phenomenon, namely the emergence of a new form of religious speculation in the post-Soviet period.

, in Cuba, the ‘speculation’ that has accompanied the rise of the Ifa cult is a product of a particular set of social and economic conditions, rather than being a sign of the ‘re-emergence of the market’, as is often suggested.
